solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: RYA sailormen deployed as part of the navy

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so these letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: Members of the Royal Yachting Association put to sea as a naval auxiliary.
explanation.walkthrough: RYA is the Royal Yachting Association, the British body for sailing; here it is just letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Marines are the amphibious infantry branch of Britain's Royal Navy.

clue.text: See 8
Help graduate at long last, to 25, 27's unacceptable breeding environment

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to help them
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the words at long is kept

explanation.surface: Someone helps a graduate at last, though some disapproving person finds the upbringing unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wilde's play, Lady Augusta Bracknell is appalled that Jack was found as a baby in a handbag at Victoria Station; her shocked cry 'A handbag?' is the play's famous line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Bracknell deems a cloakroom bag at a railway station an unthinkable place to have been born and raised from.

clue.text: Spice stick

definitions.meaning: a spice made from the dried husk of nutmeg
a ceremonial staff or club carried as a symbol of office

explanation.surface: A spice stick, like a cinnamon quill.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the nutmeg-husk seasoning and a heavy staff or club of authority.

clue.text: Rejoin desire for listeners to give up

indicators.note: what reaches the ear rather than the page, so the words are spoken

parts.note: to rejoin two things is to relink them; a desire is a wish

explanation.surface: Someone wants to rejoin a group but is told to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish is to surrender or let go of something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Daphne may be extremely naughty on speed

indicators.note: taking the extreme ends, first and last, of the word naughty

parts.note: speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: Daphne, perhaps a speeding driver, might be very naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne in Greek myth was a nymph turned into a laurel tree to escape Apollo.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is an example of a mythological nature spirit, hence the 'may be'.

clue.text: Extremes of sybaritic and arousal a public disgrace

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: 'Extremes of' carries over to this word too: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Indulgent arousal at its extremes becomes a public disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published lacks 'and', which the blog's parse needs. 'Extremes of' serves both words: the outer letters of sybaritic, then AND, then the outer letters of arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an event causing general outrage and disrepute, a public shame.

clue.text: Poor boat engine performance in believer's play

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed within the word for believer

parts.note: a theist is one who believes in God

indicators.note: a poor version is a bad, mangled one, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat's engine performs poorly in a play written by a man of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's 1895 comedy is one of the best-known stage works in English.

clue.text: Dubious drifter follows nutcase into social work

indicators.note: the combined pieces go inside the rearranged letters
to work something is to knead or reshape it, so the letters are rearranged
the wanderer comes after the nut's outer letters

parts.note: the case of the word nut is its outside letters
a rover is one who wanders or drifts

explanation.surface: A wanderer follows an eccentric into a career in social work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputed or open to argument is questionable, giving a near-synonym of doubtful.

clue.text: The man with a woman's garment, I see, reported to be Jewish

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
a bra is an undergarment worn by women

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the words sound like letters

parts.note: the two words are spoken as the letters I and C

explanation.surface: Someone notes a man in a woman's undergarment and says he is Jewish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebraic describes things relating to the Hebrews, their language or culture.

clue.text: Rock album attempt is a pain

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to make a rock album turns out to be tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is an ache in the lower back, a specific kind of bodily pain.

clue.text: Among memorabilia, displayed an epic poem

indicators.note: the letters sit among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An epic poem was on show among a collection of memorabilia.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the siege of Troy is the archetypal long heroic poem.

clue.text: Decayed tooth end is sharp

indicators.note: something decayed has broken down and fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The end of a decayed tooth is jagged and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at three o'clock sharp means exactly on time, the idiom's sense here.

clue.text: Originally born in Poland, highly skilled worker supported by both sides

indicators.note: taking the original, first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A Polish-born craftsman wins backing from both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipartisan measure has the agreement of two opposing political parties.

clue.text: Aggressive dog savaged a cousin

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: something savaged has been mauled and torn up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fierce dog attacked someone's cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugnacious means quarrelsome and eager to fight, a synonym of hostile.

clue.text: What altar boy shares with falsetto voice

parts.words: What altar boy shares with falsetto
parts.note: the letters A, L, T and O appear in that order in both altar boy and falsetto

explanation.surface: Asks what a choirboy at the altar has in common with a singer's falsetto.
explanation.walkthrough: The common ground is the letter sequence, not singing: a, l, t then o run through both altar boy and falsetto.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a vocal range, the low female or high male singing part.

clue.text: Amount halved with anything natural

indicators.note: half of the word amount is cut away, its first three letters

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Some amount, halved, comes out with anything natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Untaught ability is innate, not learned, so it is inborn rather than acquired.

clue.text: Film dance

definitions.meaning: a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance

explanation.surface: A film about dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a spool of cinema film and a brisk Scottish country dance.

clue.text: See 8
Mother is on settee with no clothes or property

parts.note: ma is an informal name for one's mother

indicators.note: stripped of its covering letters, the outermost ones at each end

explanation.surface: Mum is lying naked on the sofa, with no clothes or belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat on two floors, a kind of residential home.

clue.text: Starting to rely on employer's pocket

indicators.note: taking the starting letter of each of the three words

parts.note: one who employs something uses it, so is its user; the apostrophe-s is a link

explanation.surface: Starting out, one must rely on the boss's pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is slang for pocketing it, often improperly.

clue.text: Evil rot set in Birmingham?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the city phrase

parts.note: Birmingham is an example of a city, hence the question mark

indicators.note: set in its sense of arranged or placed in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether the rot of wickedness has taken hold in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is England's second city, in the West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an act of great wickedness, the noun sense of evil.

clue.text: Sound prison

definitions.meaning: a short sharp ring, as of glasses touched

explanation.surface: A sound prison, one that holds its inmates securely.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the ring of metal or glass and slang for a jail.

clue.text: Nose job after a long time

definitions.note: singular in the clue while the answer is plural; both name a vast stretch

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the a
a nose job reshapes the nose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets a nose job after waiting a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immeasurably long periods, so the plural means an age.

clue.text: Boy's sorry end: entire summer month with a gorgon

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the end of the word sorry is its last letter

parts.note: August is a whole month of summer, in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: A lad's sorry fate: a whole summer month spent with a fearsome woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wilde's play, Lady Augusta Bracknell, Gwendolen's mother, is called a gorgon by Algernon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorgon is a terrifying, formidable woman, which this domineering aunt epitomises.

clue.text: Terribly sectarian, but not as idiots

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: read as the plural of the letter a, so two of them are taken out

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict: bigoted sectarians are no better than idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not as' asks for the two A's of sectarian to go before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretins is an offensive term for stupid people, a synonym of fools.

clue.text: See 25
Most impressed by markets not reacting

indicators.note: the letters react, recombining as in chemistry, into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is very impressed that the markets stayed calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken by storm means captivated or overwhelmed with admiration.
